RESULT [labelnoise]: Merged COCO, Objects365 and OpenImages (945 classes) into a learned 701-class space. Mean mAP was 41.9 for the learned taxonomy, 41.6 for an expert-designed one and 41.4 for GloVe name embeddings, and the learned taxonomy beat the expert one on all datasets.
US [labelnoise]: This is evidence that visual co-firing beats both human and word-embedding name matching for class alignment. For harvested weed datasets, map each source class to a cwd12 id by how a cwd12-trained detector or the BioCLIP-2 prototypes respond to its crops, and treat the class-name string only as a hint.
CORRECTION [labelnoise]: Table 3 is confirmed: 945 classes merge into 701. Mean mAP is 41.9 learned vs 41.6 expert vs 41.4 GloVe, and the learned taxonomy beats the expert one on COCO (41.9 vs 41.5), O365 (20.8 vs 20.7) and OImg (63.0 vs 62.6). The margins are small, about 0.1-0.4 AP.
